name: Squishies Pinball Theme Palettes

license.source: Generated by Stephen Forte with OpenAI image tools (2026-09) from his own prompts.
license.terms: Project-owned; use within The Squishy Pinball Machine only; no third-party assets included.

source_direction: Glossy, rounded, candy-like pinball art with a deep indigo arcade backdrop.

usage.background: Use background and playfield_base for large surfaces.
usage.rails_and_trim: Use rail_primary and rail_secondary for cabinet rails, ramps, tubes, and borders.
usage.objects: Use object_* colors for bumpers, targets, lanes, slingshots, and flippers.
usage.effects: Use glow and highlight colors for lights, trails, jackpots, and hit feedback.
usage.text: Use text_primary on dark surfaces and text_on_color on saturated surfaces.

palettes.name: Neon Candy Baseline
palettes.role: Closest match to the supplied reference image.

palettes.name: Grape Jam
palettes.role: Darker, more purple-forward night mode with strong premium arcade energy.

palettes.name: Aqua Pool
palettes.role: Cooler, friendlier daytime-feeling palette; good for a second table or level.

palettes.name: Sherbet Sunrise
palettes.role: Warm, playful, high-visibility palette that makes the squishies feel extra soft and edible.

godot_notes.conversion: Godot can consume the hex strings directly with Color("#RRGGBB").
godot_notes.recommended_material: Use roughness around 0.22-0.35 for squishy objects, metallic 0.0-0.15, and a subtle fresnel/rim-light effect.
godot_notes.recommended_lighting: Use colored omni lights sparingly: blue/cyan for ramps, magenta for bonus areas, and gold for scoring or jackpot feedback.
godot_notes.contrast_rule: Keep the playfield at least two value steps darker than active objects so the glossy shapes remain readable during motion.
godot_notes.engine_2d_interpretation: This is a 2D game (D-002). Read roughness/metallic/omni-light notes as art direction: gloss is baked into sprites, rim light = a thin additive outline shader or modulated duplicate, glows = CanvasItem modulate / Light2D sparingly.
